chief_complaint: high fever, severe headache, and neck stiffness
hpi_details: 40M presents with 24 hours of rapidly worsening headache, a fever of 39.5C, nausea, and severe pain in his neck when trying to look down. He also complains that bright lights hurt his eyes.

investigation_events.title: STAT bacterial meningitis results
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT CSF results are now available; dexamethasone and empiric antibiotics must not be delayed for head CT or lumbar puncture.

core_concepts: Classic triad: Fever, nuchal rigidity, altered mental status (though not all present simultaneously). Photophobia is common.
common_misconceptions: Waiting for LP results before starting antibiotics.
dangerous_errors: Delaying empiric antibiotics to get a CT scan or LP.
management_principles: STAT blood cultures, then immediate empiric IV antibiotics (Ceftriaxone, Vancomycin, +/- Ampicillin) and Dexamethasone.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 40M with acute onset severe headache, fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia.
reference_soap.objective: T 39.5C, HR 110. Positive Brudzinski and Kernig signs. Alert but uncomfortable.
reference_soap.plan: Blood cultures STAT. Immediate IV Ceftriaxone, Vancomycin, and Dexamethasone. Head CT then Lumbar Puncture.

learning_objectives: Recognize meningeal signs and prioritize immediate empiric antibiotics.

teaching.one_liner: Acute onset of fever, headache, nuchal rigidity, and photophobia requiring emergent antibiotics.

must_ask.say: Do you have a stiff neck, and does looking down or bending your neck cause pain?
Does bright light bother your eyes or make the headache worse?
How quickly did the headache come on, and is it the worst headache you've ever had?
Have you had a fever, and how high has it been?
Have you felt confused, or noticed any rash or spots on your skin?

history.answer: I have an unbearable headache, a high fever, and my neck is so stiff that looking down hurts terribly.
The fever started yesterday morning about twenty-four hours ago and has stayed high since.
My thermometer read thirty-nine point five degrees yesterday evening, and I've been shivering with intense chills.
I took ibuprofen a few hours ago, but it barely brought the fever down and didn't touch the headache.
The headache started suddenly about a day ago and quickly peaked at a nine out of ten, pounding relentlessly across my entire head.
My neck is so stiff and rigid that bending my chin toward my chest causes sharp, agonizing pain.
Yes, bright lights hurt my eyes terribly, so I have to keep my eyes squeezed shut.
No, I haven't had any cough, phlegm, sore throat, or trouble breathing.
I felt very nauseous and threw up once earlier this morning, but I don't have diarrhea or belly pain.
No burning when I pee, no need to go frequently, and no flank or lower back pain.
I feel miserable and exhausted, but my head is clear and I am completely aware of everything around me.
No, I haven't noticed any purple spots, rashes, or black scabs from bug bites on my skin.
No, I haven't had night sweats or lost any weight before getting sick yesterday.
No, I haven't felt any swollen lumps or glands in my neck, armpits, or groin.
No recent travel abroad, no hiking in the woods or fields, and no contact with animals.
No one at home or around me at the office has had a fever or severe headache recently.
No, I've never had chemotherapy, and I don't take steroids or any medications that suppress my immune system.
No artificial heart valves or heart murmurs, and I haven't had any dental work or medical procedures done recently.
No, I haven't started any new prescription drugs or supplements recently.
I am in a monogamous relationship with my wife, and I have never used injected drugs.
I honestly thought I had come down with a severe case of the flu.
I'm terrified because this is the most severe and intense headache of my entire life.
I just want strong pain relief so this pounding agony in my head stops.
I don't have any chronic illnesses like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I've never had surgery and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular daily medications, only the over-the-counter ibuprofen I took earlier today.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I do not smoke and have never used tobacco or vape products.
I only drink one or two beers on the weekend occasionally.
I work as an office clerk at an IT firm and live in an apartment with my wife.
Both of my parents are healthy and there is no family history of neurologic or serious genetic disorders.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, pulse 110 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, body temperature 39.5°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Acutely ill-appearing and flushed, lying still with eyes shielded from ambient light, alert but in evident distress.
Both tympanic membranes are intact and pearly gray without erythema, fluid, or bulging.
Posterior oropharynx is pink and moist without exudate, erythema, or tonsillar swelling.
No lymphadenopathy palpable in the anterior or posterior cervical chains.
Vesicular breath sounds clear bilaterally with no rales, wheezes, or rhonchi.
Tachycardic with regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2 present, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard.
Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended without guarding or rebound tenderness.
Warm and flushed skin without petechiae, purpura, maculopapular rash, or eschars.
Alert, fully oriented to person, place, and time, with intact attention and fluent speech.
Prominent nuchal rigidity with severe resistance to passive neck flexion; positive Brudzinski and Kernig signs.
